comments.text_zh: 我认为这个讲座（[VIDEO]）应该成为任何试图通过更多自动化来提升飞行安全的人的必看内容。我认为我们已经在面临收益递减，而要消除因过度依赖自动化系统造成的事故，唯一办法就是把飞行员完全移出回路。即便在通用航空领域，容易摘到的果子也在别处。话虽如此，这仍然相当酷，我能想象类似的东西会成为某个大得多的全自动飞行管理系统的一个组成部分。编辑：链接应该已经修复。如果我仍然搞砸了，讲座的标题是“Children of the Magenta Line”。
comments.text: I think this lecture ( [VIDEO] ) should be mandatory for anyone trying to improve flight safety with more automation. I think we're already at diminishing returns, and the only way to eliminate accidents caused by over-reliance on automated systems is to cut the pilot out of the loop entirely. Even in general aviation, the low-hanging fruit is elsewhere. That said, this is still pretty cool, and I could see something like it being one component of a much larger fully automated flight management system. Edit: link should be fixed. If I'm still crushing it, the title of the lecture is "Children of the Magenta Line."

comments.why_zh: 为什么飞行员在紧急情况下会降到较低的自动化等级
comments.quote_zh: 如果你想了解更多，可以看看 Children of the Magenta Line
comments.text_zh: 这其实是正确的思路！当高级自动化让你失望时，在关键时刻摆弄高级系统很可能要了你的命。调试要花几分钟，而不是几秒钟。这就是为什么飞行员被训练成在必要时从高等级自动化降到较低等级。就像大多数关于驾驶飞机的经验教训一样，这个洞见是用大量鲜血换来的。如果你想了解更多，可以看看 Children of the Magenta Line：[VIDEO]
comments.text: It's actually the right way of thinking! When high-level automation fails you, messing around with the high-level system in a critical moment would probably be your death. Debugging takes minutes not seconds. This is why pilots are trained to drop from a high level automation to a lower one when necessary. Like most learnings about piloting, this insight was purchased with a lot of blood. If you want to know more, check out Children of the Magenta Line: [VIDEO]

comments.author: wat10000
comments.story_title: Why was there a wall near runway at S Korea plane crash airport?
comments.why_zh: 这个出色的讲座讲的是飞行员重新设置 autopilot 而不是直接接管操纵
comments.quote_zh: 一个很棒的讲座专门讲这个，叫 Children of the Magenta Line。
comments.text_zh: 这类事情过去有很多例子。航空自动化真的很难做对。如果自动化可能失效，那飞行员就必须能完成它原本要做的事。如果自动化很少失效，飞行员就可能得不到足够的练习。但如果自动化通常比飞行员做得更好，那让他们在真实航班上多练习就会产生矛盾。一个比较近的例子是 Asiana 在旧金山的坠机。当时他们几乎拥有完美的手动目视进近条件，但他们疏于练习，跟不上飞机的状态，然后情况就一步步恶化了。有一个很棒的讲座专门讲这个，叫 Children of the Magenta Line。洋红色线指的是 autopilot 上的飞行路径或方向指示，讲座讨论的是那些不停重新设置 autopilot 来引导飞机、而不是直接接管操纵的飞行员。[VIDEO]
comments.text: There are numerous past examples of this sort of thing. Automation in aviation is really hard to get right. If the automation can fail then the pilots need to be able to perform whatever it was going to do. If the automation fails rarely then the pilots may not get enough practice. But if the automation normally does a better job than the pilots, there’s a tension with letting them get more practice on real flights. A recent(ish) example is the Asiana crash in SF. They had pretty much perfect conditions for a hand-flown visual approach, but they were out of practice, got behind the airplane, and it snowballed. There’s an excellent lecture about this called Children of the Magenta Line. The magenta line being the flight path or direction indicator on an autopilot, and the discussion is about pilots who constantly reconfigure the autopilot to direct the plane instead of just taking over. [VIDEO]

comments.text_zh: Bainbridge [1] 很有意思，但已经过时。稍晚一些、更有用的同类讨论是《Children of the Magenta》[2]，一位航空公司首席飞行员在和自己的飞行员谈驾驶舱自动化以及如何使用它。需要具备一点航空术语的基本概念。自那以后已经有所进步。尽管细节没有被广泛公开，但已有足够多的 F-22、F-35 或 Gripen 飞行员谈论过现代战斗机驾驶舱自动化是什么样。战斗机飞行员的真正工作是战斗并赢得战斗，而不是驾驶飞机。大量精力被投入简化驾驶飞机这项工作，好让飞行员专注于击杀目标。如今的一般理念是，飞行员把机头指向正确方向，控制系统负责处理细节。有 F-22 飞行员被引述说，作为一种飞行器，F-22 远没有 Cessna 那么娇气。对于有 VTOL 构型（B）和航母着舰构型（C）的 F-35，人们投入了大量精力让 VTOL 着陆和航母着舰变得容易。不是因为飞行员学不会，而是因为训练往往过度执着于这些任务。Harrier（此前唯一成功的 VTOL 战斗机）的难点在于学会让这头不稳定的猛兽着陆而不坠毁。Harrier 仍然有很多坠毁事故。海军飞行员训练的难点是在航母甲板上着舰。这两项任务都与真正去咬敌人一口的工作毫无关系
comments.text: Bainbridge [1] is interesting, but dated. A more useful version of that discussion from slightly later is "Children of the Magenta", [2] an airline chief pilot talking to his pilots about cockpit automation and how to use it. Requires a basic notion of aviation jargon. There's been progress since then. Although the details are not widely publicized, enough pilots of the F-22, F-35, or the Gripen have talked about what modern fighter cockpit automation is like. The real job of fighter pilots is to fight and win battles, not drive the airplane. A huge amount of effort has been put into simplifying the airplane driving job so the pilot can focus on killing targets. The general idea today is that the pilot puts the pointy end in the right direction and the control systems take care of the details. An F-22 pilot has been quoted as saying that the F-22 is far less fussy than a Cessna as a flying machine. For the F-35, which has a VTOL configuration (B) and a carrier-landing configuration (C), much effort was put into making VTOL landing and carrier landing easy. Not because pilots can't learn to do it, but because training tended to obsess on those tasks. The hard part of Harrier (the only previous successful VTOL fighter) was learning to land the unstable beast without crashing. There were still a lot of Harrier crashes. The hard part of Naval aviator training is landing on a carrier deck. Neither of these tasks has anything to do with the real job of taking a bite out of the enem

comments.text_zh:
美国航空公司机长 Warren Van Der Burgh 在 1997 年有一个相对知名的演讲，叫“Children of Magenta”，谈到机组过度依赖屏幕上自动驾驶仪那品红色引导线的风险：* [VIDEO] * [LINK] * [LINK] 驾驶舱自动化的一些优缺点：* [LINK] 一般来说，自动化存在于一个谱系上，飞行员应该能够根据情况选择其层级：
> 在 Van 的演讲中，他描述了三个自动化层级：
> *飞行员手动驾驶飞机。
> *飞行员使用飞行指引仪、自动驾驶仪和自动驾驶模式来让飞机飞行一小段时间。例如：航向选择、飞行高度层改变、垂直速度、指示空速等。
> *飞行员使用 FMS 命令自动驾驶仪让飞机飞行数小时。
* [LINK]
comments.text: There is relatively well-know presentation from 1997 by American Airlines captain Warren Van Der Burgh called "Children of Magenta" that talked about the risk of crew being too dependent on the guiding magenta-colored lines of the autopilot on their screens: * [VIDEO] * [LINK] * [LINK] Some of the pros and cons of cockpit automation: * [LINK] Generally automation exists on a spectrum, and the pilot should be able to select its level depending on the circumstances: > In Van’s presentation he describes three levels of automation: > *The pilot manually flying the aircraft. > *The pilot using the flight director, autopilot, and autopilot modes to fly the aircraft for a short period of time. For example: Heading select, Flight Level Change, Vertical Speed, Indicated Airspeed, etc. > *The pilot using the FMS to command the autopilot to fly the aircraft for hours at a time. * [LINK]

comments.quote_zh: 人必须小心，针对特定情况保持恰当的自动化程度和控制水平
comments.text_zh: > 开车并不需要物理学的高级学位。它大多是一堆相当平常的任务拼凑在一起。一般来说这没错，但当它变得不平常时，可能转眼之间就变得很不平常。这就是为什么我有时会怀疑那些说“x% 的飞机坠毁是人为失误”的统计数据。也许吧，但等到人类介入时，自动化系统往往早已举起双手，并在数字层面惊呼“耶稣来掌舵吧”。我认为让计算机接管那些平常的部分，可能有助于改善碰撞率，因为人们会被单调乏味弄得麻木和无聊。人必须小心，针对特定情况保持恰当的自动化程度和控制水平，正如著名的“Children of the Magenta Line”演讲所说：* [VIDEO] > “Children of the magenta line”已成为一种简称，用来指那些管理和监控系统、却缺乏以权威姿态驾驶飞机的 stick-and-rudder 技能的飞行员。你可能会在关于“真正的飞行员”与“如今这些孩子”的讨论中听到它被当作贬义词使用。但在如今许多驾驶舱里，自动化文盲或许和自动化依赖一样危险。Vanderburgh 的洞见不应驱使我们去彻底拒绝自动化，而应把它放在我们飞行员工具箱中恰当的位置。正如你应该定期手动飞行以保持自己的 stick-and-rudder 技能锋利，你也应该练习使用你所飞飞机上可用的技术。* [LINK] * [LINK] * [LINK] * [LINK]
comments.text: > Driving doesn’t require an advanced degree in physics. It’s mostly a mish mash of fairly mundane tasks. Generally not wrong, but when it becomes non-mundane, it can become so in a hurry. This is why I'm sometimes skeptical about statistics that say " x% of airplane crashes are human error ". Well maybe, but by the time the humans get involved the automated systems have often thrown up their proverbial hands and digitally exclaimed " Jesus take the wheel ". I think having computers take over the mundane parts may help collision rates as people can get numbed and bored by the monotony. One has to be careful about having the right level of automation and control for the given situation, as per the famous "Children of the Magenta Line" presentation: * [VIDEO] > “Children of the magenta line” has become shorthand for pilots who manage and monitor systems but lack the stick-and-rudder skills to fly the airplane with authority. You may hear it wielded as an epithet in a discussion of “real pilots” versus “kids these days.” But in many cockpits today, automation illiteracy may be as dangerous as automation dependency. Vanderburgh’s insights shouldn’t drive us to reject automation altogether, but rather put it in its proper place in our pilot toolkits. Just as you should hand-fly regularly to keep your stick-and-rudder skills sharp, you should also practice using the technology available in the aircraft you fly. * [LINK] * [LINK] * [LINK] * [LINK]

comments.quote_zh: 依赖自动化的飞行员让他们的飞机比本应做到的更接近包线边缘
comments.text_zh: 没有专业知识的普通观察者和资本/所有者往往都会把责任归咎于操作员……只是原因各不相同。事故研究，尤其是像 _Normal Accidents_[1] 这样的书，反驳了这种假设：“……它主张把技术故障当作高度交互系统的产物来考察，并强调组织和管理因素是故障的主要原因。技术灾难不再能归因于孤立的设备故障、操作员失误或天灾。”人们普遍接受——我也相信——在 Air France 447 航班上存在大量操作员失误，但没有一个是不可预测或离奇的，而且他们被要求操作的那套系统设计糟糕，还无益地隐藏了层层复杂性，这些复杂性在巨大的“production pressure”下突然重新显现。但别只听我说——我援引权威[2]：“依赖自动化的飞行员让他们的飞机比本应做到的更接近包线边缘……”[3]。或者：@ 14:15：“……我们看到依赖自动化的机组，对自己驾驶飞机的能力缺乏信心，转而求助于自动驾驶……”[4]。[1] [LINK] [2] Captain Vanderburgh [3] Children of Magenta: [LINK] [4] [VIDEO]
comments.text: Both unsophisticated lay observers and capital/owners tend to fault operators ... for different reasons. Accident studies and, in particular, books like _Normal Accidents_[1] push back on this assumptions: "... It made the case for examining technological failures as the product of highly interacting systems, and highlighted organizational and management factors as the main causes of failures. Technological disasters could no longer be ascribed to isolated equipment malfunction, operator error, or acts of God." It is well accepted - and I believe - that there were a multitude of operator errors during the Air France 447 flight but none of them were unpredictable or exotic and the system they were tasked with operating was poorly designed and unhelpfully hid layers of complexity that suddenly re-emerged during tremendous "production pressure". But don't take my word for it - I appeal to authority[2]: "Automation dependent pilots allowed their airplanes to get much closer to the edge of the envelope than they should have ..."[3]. or: @ 14:15: "... we see automation dependent crews, lacking confidence in their own ability to fly an airplane are turning to ther autopilot ..."[4]. [1] [LINK] [2] Captain Vanderburgh [3] Children of Magenta: [LINK] [4] [VIDEO]
